comments: Looks like the failure in `testCancelFailedSearchWhenPartialResultDisallowed` is that the search thread is unable to start for over 30 seconds. Does not seem to reproduce locally. Could be just slow test runner?

@smalyshev I don't think that's it. There's no way the task doesn't get going within 30s I think. I'd look into whether either there's not enough threads available for starting that task (i.e. all search threads are blocked but we still need another search thread to start) or the task finished before we put whatever blocking we use in this test in place. We've had trouble like that with this exact test before I believe.

@original-brownbear yes, these reasons sound plausible. Any suggestions what can be done to this test to stop failing? Looking at the dashboard, the failures are not frequent (~0.1%) but the pattern is consistent...

Which suggests the failure happens because in one `assertBusy` pass it's not cancelled yet, but in the next it's already cancelled and gone.

Ok looks like what is happening here is that we start 2<=N<=5 shards one of which is supposed to throw an exception and others to sit on the lock and wait. However, if those others never even get to the lock, then they are cancelled when the exception is thrown and nothing is left for `assertBusy` to pick up. So we need to wait until at least one thread enters the lock area before throwing.

review_comments: Maybe we could make this slightly simpler by using a n`AtomicReference<CountDownLatch>` and then doing something like  `latch =  getAndSet(null); if (latch != null) latch.await` to save a variable?
Not sure I understood how it should work. I think it's better to check if this one works and then if it fixes the issues then we can refactor it.
